venture.concept: AI guided fitness subscription that brings meals, warm-ups, exercise, stretches and reminders into one app.
venture.primary_product: Personalized fitness and meal planning app
venture.target_customers: Busy adults with limited time; earlier notes also mention stable income and all ages.
venture.value_proposition: One place to manage a fitness journey, with practical guidance around the user’s goals and schedule.
venture.geographic_market: Global ambition stated by the founder
distribution_channels: iOS and Android stores and direct web subscriptions (research assumptions, not confirmed launch choices)
venture.differentiation_status: Proposed and unproven. Bundling and personalization already exist in competitors.
research_assumptions: US pricing in USD is used as a comparable market slice; it is not a decision to abandon the global ambition.
The latest busy-adult target supersedes the earlier all-ages segment.
No venture name, final platforms, launch country, costs or willingness-to-pay results were supplied.
venture.prior_research_context: Workspace reports a small App Store review sample and a food-data completeness exercise. These were not revalidated. The AI focus group is fictional and supports hypotheses only.

comparison.scope: Subscription cost benchmarks across overlapping services, not feature-equivalent products or a market-wide price estimate.
comparison.primary_rule: One verified non-promotional monthly representative per competitor. Exclude MyFitnessPal Premium+, free access, alternate SKUs, bundles, gifts, lifetime and multi-user Fitbod plans.
comparison.annual_rule: Same representative products, annual billing, separate from monthly statistics. Divide annual amounts by 12 only for effective monthly costs.
comparison.sensitivity_rule: Adds partially verified MyFitnessPal Premium+; directional only.

ranges.basis: Paid standalone observed offers, normalized to USD/month; includes alternate SKUs and partially verified prices where present. Excludes free, bundles, multi-user plans and promotions.

preliminary_pricing_recommendation.status: Preliminary hypothesis for testing, not an optimal price
preliminary_pricing_recommendation.rationale: Near Fitbod monthly pricing, above Apple Fitness+, and below Centr. Annual range straddles Fitbod and stays below Centr. Integrated reliable planning must justify a premium over narrower low-cost alternatives.
requirements: Validate willingness to pay with real busy adults
Measure AI inference, nutrition-data, support and acquisition costs
Test retention and annual-plan discount before committing
preliminary_pricing_recommendation.value_justification: Reduce daily planning with a single schedule for practical meals, warm-ups and exercise; use transparent nutritional data and reliable app performance.

market_opportunities.observation: Centr already bundles training and nutrition; MyFitnessPal already personalizes meal planning.
market_opportunities.interpretation: All-in-one or AI alone is insufficient differentiation. Test schedule-aware replanning around missed sessions and familiar household meals.

market_opportunities.observation: Annual plans are cheaper per month but require an upfront commitment.
market_opportunities.interpretation: Test a clear monthly option and a transparent annual renewal price for time-poor adults.

market_opportunities.observation: Apple offers family sharing, and Fitbod sells Duo and Family plans.
market_opportunities.interpretation: Household customization could matter, but household access itself is not a unique feature.

market_opportunities.observation: The venture workspace reports reliability concerns and nutrition-data gaps.
market_opportunities.interpretation: Prioritize stable logging and clear missing-data flags. These are product hypotheses, not demonstrated market demand.

research_limitations: Four purposively selected competitors do not represent the entire global market. Prices are a US/USD snapshot checked October 27, 2026.
Public listings were inspected without purchasing. Taxes, localized offers, eligibility, checkout totals and grandfathered plans remain uncertain.
MyFitnessPal Premium+ price observations rely on search results for an April 2025 official article and are Partially Verified. The US App Store lists several Premium prices with unclear eligibility.
Centr quarterly billing wording conflicts with one renewal sentence, and the pricing page contains a stock widget. Verify billing and checkout availability before purchase.
Fitbod lifetime price and current availability are unavailable. A crossed-out gift reference price does not prove historical sales.
Services differ in scope, device requirements and household access; monetary normalization does not establish equal value.
Competitor features are vendor claims, not independent testing. Absence from reviewed pages is not proof that a competitor lacks a feature.
The venture name, final launch market, costs, acquisition economics, retention and human willingness to pay remain unknown.
The workspace contains fictional AI focus-group responses and small secondary research samples. These do not establish customer demand or optimal price.
